note: حللت واجبك narrows the meaning to 'solved your homework'; أنجزت matches general 'did your homework'.
proposed_target: هل أنجزت واجبك بنفسك؟
proposed_english: Did you do your homework by yourself?

note: بالباص is colloquial/loan-register; use standard MSA بالحافلة.
proposed_target: هل تذهب إلى المدرسة بالحافلة؟
proposed_english: Do you go to school by bus?

note: Arabic asks whether the person wants to advise; English asks whether they have advice.
proposed_target: هل لديك أي نصيحة لي؟
proposed_english: Do you have any advice for me?

note: Standard spelling is الانتظار, not الإنتظار.
proposed_target: كل ما عليك القيام به هو الانتظار.
proposed_english: All you need to do is wait.

note: Standard collocation is مساعدتك في إيجاد عمل.
proposed_target: أستطيع مساعدتك في إيجاد عمل.
proposed_english: I can help you find a job.

note: Arabic uses ذلك ('that'); English says 'this' and uses a less direct construction.
proposed_target: لا أعرف كيف يُفعل ذلك.
proposed_english: I don't know how that is done.

note: Word order is unnatural in standard MSA; حتى should scope أعرف naturally.
proposed_target: أنا لا أعرف حتى ما ذلك.
proposed_english: I don't even know what that is.

note: في بتناول is malformed by doubled prepositions.
proposed_target: لا أرغب في تناول أي طعام اليوم.
proposed_english: I don't feel like eating anything today.

note: Standard orthography requires للأكل الآن.
proposed_target: ليس لدي وقت للأكل الآن.
proposed_english: I don't have time to eat now.

note: ما أفعله means 'what I do'; English is infinitival 'what to do'.
proposed_target: لا أعرف ماذا أفعل غدًا.
proposed_english: I don't know what to do tomorrow.

note: English adds 'just', absent from Arabic.
proposed_target: لا أعلم ماذا أقول.
proposed_english: I don't know what to say.

note: Arabic is present أريد; English is past 'wanted'.
proposed_target: أريد فقط أن تساعدني.
proposed_english: I just want you to help me.

note: Current Arabic is misspelled and future ('won't do this'), while English is past ('didn't do that').
proposed_target: أعلم أنك لم تفعل ذلك.
proposed_english: I know that you didn't do that.

note: Standard spelling is الذي, not الذى.
proposed_target: أنا أعرف ما الذي تحاول فعله.
proposed_english: I know what you're trying to do.

note: Arabic كنت أعلم ... ستقول is past 'I knew you would say'; English is present/future.
proposed_target: كنت أعلم أنك ستقول لا.
proposed_english: I knew you would say no.

note: Current Arabic says 'I will never say no to you'; English says past inability 'I never could'.
proposed_target: لم أستطع قط أن أقول لك لا.
proposed_english: I never could say no to you.

note: Current phrasing أنه الوقت لشرب is awkward; use standard حان الوقت.
proposed_target: أظن أن الوقت قد حان لشرب شيء ما.
proposed_english: I think it's time for a drink.

note: Missing initial hamza in أعتقد.
proposed_target: أعتقد بأنه يمكننا مساعدة بعضنا البعض.
proposed_english: I think we can help each other.

note: Missing hamzas and Arabic merely says 'wouldn't come'; English says 'would never come'.
proposed_target: اعتقدت أنك لن تأتي إلى هنا أبدًا.
proposed_english: I thought you would never come here.

note: Direct contradiction: Arabic says 'I don't know where she went'; English says 'I want to know'.
proposed_target: أريد أن أعرف إلى أين ذهبت.
proposed_english: I want to know where she went.

note: Current phrase is ungrammatical and misspells بإمكانك; use a standard help + على construction.
proposed_target: ربما يمكنك مساعدتي على فعل ذلك.
proposed_english: Maybe you can help me do that.

note: Standard spelling is الاتصال, not الإتصال.
proposed_target: بلغها أن تعاود الاتصال بي من فضلك.
proposed_english: Please tell her to call me back.

note: إلى أي مكان أذهب is awkward; إلى أين is standard and directly matches 'where'.
proposed_target: أخبرني من فضلك إلى أين أذهب بعد ذلك.
proposed_english: Please tell me where to go next.
